summary: Maximum average of any contiguous subarray of length k.
mainInsight: Maintain the sum of a fixed-size window: add the entering element and subtract the leaving one. Track the maximum sum and divide by k once at the end.

approaches.name: Fixed-size sliding window
approaches.summary: Update the window sum in O(1) per step.

cards.answer: Fixed-size sliding window sum: add the entering element and subtract the leaving one. Clue: It asks for the best average over contiguous subarrays of one fixed length k, so slide a window of size k and update its sum incrementally.

cards.explanation: Moving the window changes only two elements, so its sum is updated in constant time and the maximum sum gives the maximum average.

promptVariants: Which technique avoids recomputing the sum of every window?
How do you slide from one window of size k to the next?
options: Add the entering element, drop the leaving one
Sort the array and take the k largest elements
Binary search on the best possible average value
Keep a heap of the k best windows seen so far
cards.answer: Add the entering element, drop the leaving one
cards.explanation: Each step changes the window sum by nums[i] - nums[i - k], so every window costs O(1).

incorrectOptionExplanations.Sort the array and take the k largest el: The subarray must be contiguous; sorting destroys the order.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Binary search on the best possible avera: That is a harder variant (the length is not fixed there); not needed here.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Keep a heap of the k best windows seen s: A heap does not preserve contiguity and adds a log factor.

promptVariants: Why compare sums rather than averages while sliding?
When should the division by k happen, and why is it safe to compare window sums instead of averages?
cards.answer: All windows have the same length k, so comparing sums gives the same ordering as comparing averages. Divide once at the end, which avoids repeated floating point work and rounding noise.
cards.explanation: Integer sums are exact in Python.
One pass after the initial window.

promptVariants: What does the algorithm return for nums = [-3,-5] and k = 2?
nums = [-3,-5], k = 2: which window is examined and what is returned?
options: -4.0: the only window is the whole array
0.0: there is no full window yet
An error: there is no element to subtract
-2.0: the sum is divided by k twice
cards.answer: -4.0: the only window is the whole array
cards.explanation: When k == n the initial window is the only window, so the sliding loop never runs and -8 / 2 = -4.0 is returned.

incorrectOptionExplanations.0.0: there is no full window yet: The first loop builds exactly one full window of length k.
incorrectOptionExplanations.An error: there is no element to subtrac: range(k, len(nums)) is empty, so the sliding loop simply does not run.
incorrectOptionExplanations.-2.0: the sum is divided by k twice: The window sum -8 is divided by k once at the end: -8 / 2 = -4.0.
